Water pooling against a foundation is one of the most expensive problems a house can have. The common building-code guideline is that ground should fall at least **6 inches over the first 10 feet** from the house (about 5%). You can check it in an afternoon.

**How to measure:** drive a stake against the foundation and another 10 ft (3 m) out. Tie a string between them and level it with a line level. At each stake, measure from the string down to the ground. The drop is the outer measurement minus the inner one. Repeat every 10–15 ft along each wall.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="fg"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  HM.tool({
    id: 'fg', step: 'Your measurements',
    inputs: [
      { k: 'dist', l: 'Distance between the stakes', t: 'len', d: { us: 10, si: 3 }, w: 3 },
      { k: 'wall', l: 'Length of this wall', t: 'len', w: 3 },
      { k: 'drops', l: 'Drop at each spot, comma-separated (use a minus sign if the ground rises away from the house)', t: 'list', of: 'dep', ph: u => u === 'us' ? 'e.g. 6.5, 4, 1, -1' : 'e.g. 16, 10, 2.5, -2' }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const ds = v.drops || [];
      if (!(v.dist > 0) || !ds.length) return U.empty('Enter the stake distance and at least one drop.');
      const need = 0.05 * v.dist; // m
      const seg = v.wall > 0 ? v.wall / ds.length : null;
      let vol = 0, bad = 0;
      const rows = ds.map((d, i) => {
        const s = d / v.dist * 100, ok = d >= need - 1e-6;
        if (!ok) { bad++; if (seg) vol += (need - d) * v.dist / 2 * seg; }
        return `<tr><td>${i + 1}</td><td>${U.f(d, 'dep', 1)}</td><td>${HM.fmt(s, 1)}%</td><td>${ok ? '<span class="tag good">OK</span>' : d <= 0 ? '<span class="tag bad">Slopes toward house</span>' : `<span class="tag warn">Raise ${U.f(need - d, 'dep', 1)}</span>`}</td></tr>`;
      });
      let h = bad === 0 ? U.big('Result', 'Grade looks good', `Every spot falls at least ${U.f(need, 'dep', 1)} over ${U.f(v.dist, 'len', 0)}.`)
        : U.big('Result', `${bad} of ${ds.length} spots need work`, `The guideline is a fall of at least ${U.f(need, 'dep', 1)} over ${U.f(v.dist, 'len', 0)}.`);
      h += `<table class="tt"><thead><tr><th>Spot</th><th>Drop</th><th>Slope</th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody>${rows.join('')}</tbody></table>`;
      const work = [`Required drop = 5% × ${U.f(v.dist, 'len', 1)} = ${U.f(need, 'dep', 1)}`];
      if (bad && seg) {
        const order = vol * 1.25;
        h += U.kv([['Fill soil to fix (approx.)', `${U.f(order, 'vol', 2)} (${U.f(order, 'cuft', 0)})`]]);
        work.push(`Each low spot is raised at the wall and tapered to nothing at the outer stake: a wedge of (shortfall × ${U.f(v.dist, 'len', 1)} ÷ 2) × ${U.f(seg, 'len', 1)} of wall`, `Total wedge volume = ${U.f(vol, 'vol', 2)}; +25% for compaction = ${U.f(order, 'vol', 2)}`);
      } else if (bad) h += U.note('Enter the wall length to estimate how much fill it takes.');
      if (bad) {
        h += `<h3>How to fix it</h3><ul class="plain"><li>Build the slope with a <strong>compactable, clay-rich fill</strong>, tamped in layers. Topsoil, mulch and sand let water straight through to the foundation.</li><li>Finish with a thin layer of topsoil to grow on.</li><li>Keep at least 6 in (15 cm) between the soil and siding or any wood, and never bury weep holes or vents. If raising the soil would break this rule, use a swale (a shallow channel) to carry water away instead.</li><li>Extend downspouts at least 5–10 ft (1.5–3 m) from the house.</li></ul>`;
      }
      h += U.note('Local codes and site conditions vary. If water is already getting into a basement, or the house sits close to a property line, get a professional to look at it.');
      return { html: h, work };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Other signs of a grading problem

- Water standing next to the foundation after rain or irrigation.
- Mulch or soil piled up against the siding, often built up over years.
- Downspouts that empty right at the wall.
- Patios, walks or window wells that have settled so they tip toward the house.
- Damp patches, efflorescence (white crust) or musty smells in a basement or crawlspace.

Most of these are cheap to fix compared with foundation repairs.
